title: Quantum-CPA Security of Key-Alternating Ciphers
summary: In the quantum-CPA model, whitening keys do not strengthen FX, while finding attacks on key-alternating ciphers or ruling them out in general remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the quantum-CPA model, whitening keys in the FX construction do not increase security, but the security of key-alternating ciphers remains unresolved. Key-alternating ciphers are multiple-round generalizations of the Even--Mansour construction, and popular ciphers, most importantly AES, follow this design principle. Determine their quantum-CPA security by either designing quantum algorithms that break key-alternating ciphers or showing that such attacks are not possible in general.

scope.domain: Quantum cryptanalysis of key-alternating block ciphers, which generalize the Even–Mansour construction to multiple rounds.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether quantum algorithms can break key-alternating ciphers or whether such attacks can be ruled out in general.

citations.label: Grover Meets Simon - Quantumly Attacking the FX-construction

progress.summary: After showing that whitening keys do not increase FX security in the quantum-CPA model, the paper presents the security of multi-round key-alternating ciphers as its first and possibly most important open problem. It calls for either quantum attacks or a general demonstration that such attacks are impossible.
citation_labels: Gregor Leander et al., Grover Meets Simon - Quantumly Attacking the FX-construction
